evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the call timeline or the promise of a dependable quote; jumped directly into probing with 'So I'll take a few pieces of information down just to make sure I get the right rate for you.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'Alright. So My biggest concern is, I think just related to the insurance part' — customer volunteered it, rep didn't proactively ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised insurance concern (damaged TV history, coverage limits, replacement vs. repair). Rep followed up: 'So honestly, I don't personally know that...' and continued with 'our movers first off, they are professionally trained...' Dug into the concern substantively across multiple exchanges.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Mentioned $2,000 coverage multiple times but framing was fragmented and incomplete. Never clearly stated 'no deductible / no fine print' or 'built into the rate, not an add-on.' Customer had to ask for clarification: 'is it 2000 to buy a new TV or is it 2000 to fix the existing TV?'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' after providing the $585 estimate. Rep said 'Alright, I do have that here' and moved directly to 'So the hourly rate for this particular move would be $204...'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' Rep closed with 'whenever you kind of come to a decision you know, definitely, you can reply to an email' — soft, optional language with no explicit ask.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Asked 'And then where would we be taking to...' which is a logistics clarification, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' Rep asked 'do we have availability on that day' — not a final concerns check.

top_strength: Strong two-layer follow-up on the customer's critical insurance concern—when the customer pressed on $2,000 coverage limits and replacement vs. repair, the rep stayed engaged and provided context about professional training, inspection protocols, and case-by-case handling rather than brushing past.
coaching_note: The call skipped the foundational quid pro quo framing entirely and never asked an explicit close ('Would you like our help?'); add both to your opening and closing to set clear expectations and create a genuine commitment moment rather than a soft email-followup trail-off.
